kinds.a: antacid · heartburn tablets · reflux remedy · acid reducer · indigestion liquid
kinds.d: Non-prescription medicine that neutralises stomach acid, forms a barrier against reflux or reduces acid production.
t: antacid (calcium carbonate, magnesium or aluminium salts, sodium bicarbonate)

kinds.a: constipation remedy · stool softener · fibre supplement · enema · glycerin suppository
kinds.d: Medicine that loosens stools or speeds bowel movement to relieve constipation, taken by mouth or given rectally.
t: medicinal enema (saline, bisacodyl); a plain enema bulb or anal douche is not a medicine

kinds.d: Non-prescription medicine that slows the gut or binds irritants to stop short-term diarrhoea.

kinds.a: ORS · rehydration sachets · electrolyte solution · oral electrolyte
kinds.d: Measured mix of glucose and salts, as powder sachets or ready-to-drink liquid, to replace fluid lost through diarrhoea or vomiting.

kinds.a: motion-sickness tablets · seasickness remedy · travel sickness patch
kinds.d: Medicine taken before a journey to prevent nausea and vomiting from motion; usually an antihistamine or hyoscine.
t: hyoscine skin patch (prescription in many countries)

brands.d: Reckitt's indigestion remedy brand, sold as liquids and chewable tablets.
Chewable calcium-carbonate antacid first produced by the Lewis-Howe Company, now made by Haleon in St. Louis.
Effervescent sodium-bicarbonate tablet, with or without aspirin, developed by Miles Laboratories and owned by Bayer since 1978.
Pink bismuth-subsalicylate liquid and tablets for upset stomach, heartburn and diarrhoea; sold as Bismosal until 1919, now Procter & Gamble.
Loperamide brand from Janssen, whose founder Paul Janssen first made the drug in 1969; sold over the counter as Imodium A-D in the US from 1988.
Psyllium-husk fibre supplement introduced by G. D. Searle and owned by Procter & Gamble since 1985.
Rehydration treatment for acute diarrhoea, described by its maker as the UK's best-selling one; made by Phoenix Labs for Dendron Brands.
Abbott's oral electrolyte solution for ill children, sold to consumers since 1969 and also used by adults.
Dimenhydrinate antihistamine for motion sickness, introduced by G.D. Searle in 1949; a meclizine Less Drowsy version is also sold.

notes: Tier shelf; no archetypes (quality-of-life medicines, no efficacy claims). Old k12 Medicinal enema folded into Laxative as the type 'medicinal enema' (Fleet model kept, with its old maker). New kinds: Indigestion & heartburn remedy, Laxative, Anti-diarrhoeal, Oral rehydration salts, Travel-sickness remedy, each sourced to a retrieved Wikipedia page (Antacid, Laxative, Antidiarrheal, Oral rehydration therapy, Motion sickness).
